question.leadin: A powerful family that ruled this city included men like Lorezno the Magnificent.
question.text: Name this Italian city once ruled by the Medici family. This city is the most populous one in Tuscany.
question.clue: Michele di Lando became gonfaloniere of justice in this city during the 1378 Ciompi Revolt, and Pope Sixtus IV backed the Pazzi conspiracy in this city.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the newspaper Avanti!
swap.text: Although he had formerly edited it, this fascist leader banned the publication of Avanti! when he took power. Nicknamed "Il Duce", he led the Blackshirts during the March on Rome.
swap.clue: This former leader and his mistress Claretta Petacci were killed by partisans in the village of Giulino di Mezzegra near Lake Como.

question.leadin: Give the following about colorful symbols throughout history.
question.text: The Redshirts were loyal supporters of this Italian unifier who led the Expedition of a Thousand and fought in the Uruguayan Civil War.
question.clue: This European declined Lincoln's request to lead the Union in the Civil War, but did lead the Hunters of the Alps against Austria.

swap.leadin: This family produced three popes, a large bank, and a giant power vacuum in Tuscany after it declined.
swap.text: Name this powerful Italian family that dominated politics in Florence for multiple centuries.
swap.clue: One member of this group excommunicated Martin Luther.

question.leadin: The League of Cambrai was formed in opposition to this city.
question.text: Name this city famed for its leaders known as doges [pronounced "doajes"] and its gondoliers, who travel along its many canals.
question.clue: This city-state's hinterland, the "Domini di Terraferma," was partitioned between Austria and the Cisalpine Republic by the provisions of the 1797 Treaty of Campo Formio.

swap.leadin: This powerful merchant republic was ruled by doges.
swap.text: Name this northern Italian merchant republic which diverted the Fourth Crusade to sack Constantinople. It was part of the Holy League that defeated the Ottomans at the Battle of the Lepanto.
swap.clue: The Treaty of Campo Formio incorporated this city into Austria, officially ending a republic founded in AD 697.

question.leadin: Unemployed veterans of a war in this region formed the Catalan Company, a band of mercenaries headquartered in Thebes.
question.text: Name this region whose namesake "vespers" resulted in the overthrow of its Capetian ruler Charles of Anjou. The Vespers resulted in the division of this region into two.
question.clue: This region names a disastrous "expedition" led by Nicias during the Peloponnesian War.

swap.text: Moro negotiated the Historic Compromise with this Italian political party. During much of the postwar period, it was the largest party of its political orientation in Western Europe.
swap.answerHtml: Italian Communist Party [or PCI; or Partito Comunista Italiano; do not accept or prompt on answers including the word "socialist"]
swap.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

question.text: This Genoese admiral and "perpetual censor" made his fame in a later Italian War by liberating Marseilles for the French. His nephew of the same last name led a fleet at Lepanto, and a ship named for him collided with the MS Stockholm in 1956.
question.clue: This man, the primary target of the Fieschi conspiracy, was depicted as the god Neptune by Agnolo Bronzino.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the reign of Spanish king Charles I.
swap.text: At this 1525 battle in northern Italy, Charles' forces recaptured Milan and took Francis I of France as prisoner.
swap.clue: Alfonso d'Avalos, the Marquis of Pescara, led the arquebusiers under the overall command of Charles de Lannoy; he breached the wall of Mirabello around midnight and many combatants drowned in the nearby Ticino River.

question.leadin: Name some things about Napoleonic puppet states.
question.text: A state named after this city was ruled by the flamboyant dandy Joachim Murat. This city was previously the center of the Parthenopean Republic, which was opposed by its lazzaroni lower class.
question.answerHtml: Naples [or Napoli; or Kingdom of Naples; accept Regno di Napoli]
question.clue: A tax on fruit prompted a fisherman to lead a rebellion in this city, in which Fabrizio Ruffio led the Papal Sanfedismo movement to overthrow the Napoleonic Parthenopean Republic.

swap.leadin: This republic fought against Venice in the War of Chioggia ("kee-OH-juh").
swap.text: Name this republic, which competed with Venice to dominate the Mediterranean in the 13thand 14thcenturies. Christopher Columbus was born in this republic, whose capital was a city in Liguria.
swap.clue: This city was led for much of its history by the Boccanegra family and was the home of admiral Andrea Doria.

question.leadin: Name these influential works of pre-modern Italy.
question.text: This monumental epic poem has Dante journey through the Inferno, Purgatory, and Paradise.

swap.text: Supported by Charles Emmanuel III, Rosa Govone organized a convitti consisting of a series of shelters and textile shops to provide work to young women throughout this duchy. Monarchs of Italy following the 19th-century reunification came from a family named for this duchy's namesake county, who ruled Piedmont-Sardinia.
swap.answerHtml: Duchy of Savoy [or Duché de Savoie or Ducato di Savoia; accept County of Savoy; accept House of Savoy or Savoyards]
swap.clue: That duke of this region married his son to the sister of Louis XIII, Christine Marie.

question.leadin: This man rose to renown after helping his brother Humphrey achieve victory at the Battle of Civitate, after which he led a rapid conquest of Sicily, where his other brother, Roger, was installed as Count in 1071.
question.text: Identify this enterprising general who sacked Rome in 1084 after Pope Gregory VII called upon him to rescue Pontiff from his imprisonment by Henry IV. This man's son, Bohemund, famously led the First Crusade through Anatolia and ruled over the city of Antioch.
question.answerHtml: Robert Guiscard [or Robert the Cunning; accept similar words for "cunning"]
question.clue: Soon after that, he reconciled with the Papacy and was invested as duke at the Council of Melfi.

swap.text: Davies listed this region as one of the title places in his Vanished Kingdoms, in which he called this place the "House that Humbert Built." This region gives its name to the family to which the kings of unified Italy belonged.
swap.clue: This historical region, home to Humbert the Whitehanded. This region lends its name to a dynasty whose rulers included Charles Albert and Umberto I.

question.text: This man's namesake "crisis" consisted of his murder by Fascist squadristi and burial outside of Rome and led to the "Aventine Succession," which did not succeed in its opposition to Mussolini.
question.clue: In his book The Fascisti Exposed, what socialist politician claimed the 1924 general election to be fraudulent? This fierce opponent of fascism was later kidnapped and murdered, triggering a namesake crisis.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Italian politics during the First World War.
swap.text: This man headed the Italian delegation to the Paris Peace Conference to round out the "Big Four." He served as prime minister of Italy from 1917 to 1919.
swap.clue: This leader who upset nationalists by failing to address the broken London Pact.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some political intrigue in Italy, FTPE.
question.text: This event's name is somewhat of a misnomer, since Francesco Salviati of Pisa was the one who solicited members of the eponymous family to have Gerolamo Riario installed as a leader of Florence.
question.clue: Frederico Montelfeltro likely had a battalion waiting in the hills during this event, which left citizens hanging from the walls of the Palazzo Vecchio and tossed into the Arno river.

swap.leadin: This man was engaged to Mathilde of Austria, who died after her dress caught on fire because of a cigarette.
swap.text: Name this King of Italy who was assassinated by Gaetano Bresci in 1900. He supported the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria-Hungary as king.
swap.clue: This ruler's lost popularity for supporting the Bava-Beccaris massacre in Milan.
